Content that touches on highly subjective or sensitive topics (politics, religion, morality) prompts divergent interpretations and thus more disagreement.
Sentences with multiple clauses or shifting subjects (complex syntax) invite disagreement by allowing multiple interpretations of which part carries the main sentiment or target.
Mentions of sensitive sociopolitical topics (e.g., race, gender, religion) tend to create disagreement because annotators differ in thresholds for what counts as hateful or inflammatory.
Texts that rely on sarcasm, irony, or deadpan humor (where the literal meaning differs from the intended meaning) are more likely to trigger annotator disagreement.
